answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can price admission in unforgeable work: every new agent must burn real compute on a one-time proof-of-work puzzle, like polishing a rough opal until its fire appears. To stop established agents from cloning themselves, the ledger should mirror each wallet's history into a reputation score that decays without honest participation. Grading works like a lantern sweep: assignments are randomized each epoch, so an attacker can never predict which peers will inspect its answers. One cheap key, one vote, and recycled identities inherit zero trust.
